To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the deconvolution of clipped ultrasonic data can be performed by solving a quadratic programming (QP) problem with inequality constraints, that this problem has a simple closed form solution, and that this solution is very accurate for low clipping distortion and can compete in accuracy for higher distortion levels with the exact solution of the deconvolution problem.

the deconvolution of ultrasonic signals that have been clipped by the analog-to-d digital converter can be performed by using the presented methods and that the deconvolved signals are useful in signal restoration.

the deconvolution of ultrasonic signals that have been clipped by the analog-to-digitial converter can be done with a quadratic programming algorithm, that the quadratic programming solution is very accurate for low clipping distortion, but becomes less accurate for larger distortion, and that a linear algorithm can be used to approximate the quadratic programming solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
deconvolution methods for ultrasonic signals that have been clipped at their maximum and minimum amplitudes, and with restoration of the clipped amplitues.
deconvolution and model based restoration of ultrasonic signals for the purpose of improving their quality and accuracy.
the development of a general approach to deconvolving ultrasonically acquired signals for which some or all of the samples have clipped.

the exact solution should be preferred in general.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methods can be successfully applied to deconvolve clipped ultrasonic signals with a good accuracy, even when the clipping levels are known only roughly.
the exact solution to the maximum a posteriori estimator for the deconvolution problem with clipping distortion yields the best performance.
the exact solution is the preferred choice for low clipping distortion, while for larger distortion levels the first approximate solution is recommended.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presented methods are simple and efficient to implement.
it is possible to obtain accurate deconvolution and restoration results even when the signal has been severely distorted.
the presented deconvolution and restoration methods provide an accurate way of analyzing clipped signals, which is of great importance in ultrasonic testing.
